BitMine Buys 17,362 ETH, Total Holdings Top 6 Million ETH

BitMine said it acquired 17,362 ETH over the past week, bringing total holdings to 6,001,302 ETH as of September 27. The position represents about 4.9% of Ethereum’s 122.1 million ETH supply, putting the company 98% of the way toward its stated goal of owning 5% of all ETH. BitMine has staked 5,067,309 ETH, or roughly 84% of its holdings, and said its total crypto, cash, marketable securities and other investments were valued at $17.2 billion. — link

Tether Expands WDK Into Africa and GCC via Shiga Partnership

Tether said Shiga will use its open-source Wallet Development Kit to launch self-custodial products supporting USD₮, Bitcoin and XAU₮ across Africa and the GCC. The rollout includes ENTA for individuals and businesses, and Pulse for banks and fintechs building products around cross-border payments, treasury and settlement flows. The collaboration follows Tether’s 2025 strategic investment in Shiga. — link

Bitget Moves $169M in BTC From Protection Fund to Hot Wallets

According to @ai_9684xtpa, 2,042.28 BTC, worth about $169 million, has been transferred from Bitget’s roughly 5,500 BTC Protection Fund into hot wallets, while another 3,457.72 BTC remains on-chain. She noted that the transfers were made in advance and should not be interpreted as actual user withdrawal volume. Bitget CEO Gracy Chen previously said the company would replenish the Protection Fund back to its $300 million baseline within a week. — link

Bitget reopens BTC withdrawals after September 24 security incident

Bitget said it has begun a phased resumption of withdrawals following the September 24 security incident, with BTC withdrawals on the Bitcoin network reopening at 08:00 UTC on September 28.
